knowledge:
- key_parameters: dbandwidth=A vector of length 2 specifying the kernel density bandwidth in the M/Z and scan directions. dbandwidth[1] must be >= dgridstep[1] and dbandwidth[2] must be >= dgridstep[2] ;; dgridstep=A vector of length 2 specifying the grid spacing in the M/Z and scan directions (defaults are 0.005 and 1; larger values like 0.01 and 1 speed up computation) ;; outfileDens=Path to an external file to save the computed density estimate. If NULL, the density is not saved. Specifying a saved file path in subsequent runs skips the time-intensive density estimation phase ;; cutoff=Density threshold for calling peak bounds in slicepi(). If NULL, a data-driven threshold is automatically identified ;; mzsubset=A vector of length 2 specifying a subset of M/Z values to process, useful for speeding up computation during testing
- alternatives: xcms and MZMine 2 are mentioned as alternatives. While they also provide preprocessing, they focus more on feature detection and alignment in individual samples, whereas yamss focuses on joint bounding of peaks across samples to improve differential analysis
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing untargeted high-throughput LC/MS metabolomics datasets where the primary goal is high-quality differential abundance analysis between experimental conditions
- pitfalls: All samples that are to be analyzed together must be processed together through bakedpi. Ensure that dbandwidth components are strictly greater than or equal to their corresponding dgridstep components to avoid binning and distance calculation errors. Density estimation can be highly time-intensive; use outfileDens to save intermediate density estimates to avoid recomputing them when adjusting peak-calling thresholds

workflows.name: lcms_preprocessing_and_differential_analysis
workflows.intent: Preprocess raw LC/MS metabolomics data, detect and quantify peaks, and perform differential abundance analysis.
input: files (vector of paths to raw mass spectrometry files, e.g., .mzML or .mzXML)
workflows.stages: 1. Read raw mass spectrometry data using readMSdata() ;; 2. Preprocess raw data and estimate bivariate kernel density using bakedpi() ;; 3. Call peak bounds and quantify peaks using slicepi() ;; 4. Perform differential abundance analysis using diffrep() ;; 5. Extract peak bounds using peakBounds() ;; 6. (Optional) Visualize density regions using plotDensityRegion()
workflows.code:
colData <- DataFrame(sampClasses = classes, ionmode = "pos")
cmsRaw <- readMSdata(files = files, colData = colData, mzsubset = c(500,520), verbose = TRUE)
cmsProc <- bakedpi(cmsRaw, dbandwidth = c(0.01, 10), dgridstep = c(0.01, 1),
                   outfileDens = NULL, dortalign = TRUE, mzsubset = c(500, 520), verbose = TRUE)
cmsSlice <- slicepi(cmsProc, cutoff = NULL, verbose = TRUE)
dr <- diffrep(cmsSlice, classes = classes)
topPeaks <- as.numeric(rownames(dr)[1:10])
bounds <- peakBounds(cmsSlice)
idx <- match(topPeaks, bounds[,"peaknum"])
bounds[idx,]
dmat <- densityEstimate(cmsProc)
mzrange <- c(bounds[idx[1], "mzmin"], bounds[idx[1], "mzmax"])
scanrange <- c(bounds[idx[1], "scanmin"], bounds[idx[1], "scanmax"])
plotDensityRegion(cmsProc, mzrange = mzrange + c(-0.5,0.5), scanrange = scanrange + c(-30,30))
cmsSlice2 <- slicepi(cmsProc, densityCutoff(cmsSlice)*0.99)
dqs <- densityQuantiles(cmsProc)
cmsSlice3 <- slicepi(cmsProc, dqs["98.5%"])
